newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia Olympics minister attacks racist element.
newsitem.headline: Australia Olympics minister attacks racist element.

text.p: Australia's recent race row is the work of fringe elements and the country's multicultural make-up will be a strength in hosting the 2000 Olympics, the chief organiser of the games said on Wednesday.

Michael Knight, New South Wales Minister for the Olympics and president of the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games, said at a lecture in Jakarta that Australia's image was being tarnished by the controversy.

In his speech, Knight did not mention by name independent Australian legislator Pauline Hanson whose campaign against immigration, multiculturalism, Aboriginal welfare and a deeper role in Asia has ignited a widely-reported and vigorous debate in Australia.
He later told reporters he was reluctant to single out Hanson personally, but "if the cap fits, she can wear it".

"Fringe elements in our society have been creating a bad and unrepresentative image of Australia, particularly in Asia," Knight said in his speech, part of The Australia Lectures series presented by Canberra's Australia-Indonesia Institute.

"It is unfortunate when sensationalist media coverage gives our neighbours the mistaken impression that Australians as a whole might embrace the xenophobic rantings of those on the extreme right of our broad political spectrum," Knight said.
He said it was important to recognise that Australia was essentially a nation of migrants and the descendants of migrants.

"We are one of the most multicultural of all nations. Indeed, this was one of Sydney's great advantages when bidding for the 2000 Olympics and will undoubtedly prove to be one of our great strengths when we welcome the world," he said.
